name: BTS6143D
title: PROFET BTS 6143 D: 10 mΩ smart high-side power switch with load current sense, PG-TO252-5-11
summary: A single-channel high-side switch for 12 V and 24 V grounded loads: an N-channel vertical power MOSFET with its own charge pump, driven by pulling current out of its input pin, in a 5-pin D-Pak. It limits current, latches off on a short circuit, shuts down and restarts on overtemperature, clamps inductive kickback and survives load dump, loss of ground and a reversed battery (during which it turns its channel on). A sense pin returns a current about 1/10 000 of the load current, and a fixed fault current when it has shut down or is overloaded. AEC qualified, RoHS compliant.

pins.function: Sense output. In normal on-state it sources a current in proportion to the load current; on overload, overtemperature or short-circuit shutdown it sources the fixed fault current IIS,fault.

circuits.title: Basic connection with input switch and sense resistor
circuits.description: Supply on Vbb, the load on OUT, an input switch that pulls IN to ground through RIN, and RIS from IS to ground so the sense current appears as the voltage VIS. Two or more of these switches can be put in parallel for more load current.
notes: U1.OUT is pins 1 and 5 joined; U1.Vbb is pin 3 and the tab.

circuits.title: Overvoltage protection of the logic part
circuits.description: Outside parts for supply surges beyond the internal 67 V zeners on IN and IS. RIN (optional) goes in series with the input. RIS takes the sense current to signal ground; RV (optional) runs from IS to the sense output, where the zener VZ,VIS (optional) clamps it to signal ground. Without RV and VZ,VIS, once the overvoltage passes 67 V typ the voltage from IS to ground can climb above 5 V.
notes: Inside the device: Rbb = 100 Ω typ in the logic supply, VZ,IN = VZ,IS = 67 V typ.

circuits.title: Reverse battery protection (Reversave)
circuits.description: With the battery the wrong way round, current flows from signal ground into IN and IS, which turns the power transistor on so the load current runs through the channel rather than the body diode. RIN sets the share through IN and RIS the share through IS; a small-signal diode D across the NPN input switch carries the input share. RIN is required when the reverse voltage is above 16 V, and the two paths together should take about 80 mA.
notes: RIN from 1/RIN + 1/RIS = 0.08 A / (|Vbb| - 12 V).

circuits.title: Inverse load current operation
circuits.description: An outside source holds OUT above Vbb (VOUT > Vbb > 0 V), so the load current IL runs backwards from OUT to Vbb. The input switch and RIS are connected as usual; in this mode the sense current is zero.

circuits.title: Vbb disconnect with an energised inductive load, version a
circuits.description: If the supply is opened while an inductive load carries current, that current needs a path of its own. A diode D1 and a zener DZ1, anodes joined, across the load from OUT to ground provide it. With RIN = 0 the sum VZL + VD must stay below 39 V; a higher clamp is allowed only when the IN and IS currents are held to 120 mA. A plain diode, a zener or a varistor can serve instead.

circuits.title: Short circuit test circuit
circuits.description: The supply feeds Vbb through a primary impedance of 10 mΩ and 5 µH. From OUT a secondary inductance LSC and resistance RSC run to a load ZL; closing switch SC shorts the far end of RSC to ground. The allowable RSC against LSC curves are for this setup.

circuits.title: Inductive load switch-off energy dissipation
circuits.description: An inductive load, L in series with RL, hangs from OUT; the input is switched by IIN and RIS loads IS. When the input opens, OUT is clamped VON(CL) below Vbb and the device absorbs EAS: the energy taken from the supply while the load demagnetises, plus the energy stored in L, less the energy burnt in RL.

operation.text: One N-channel vertical power FET with a charge pump, built chip on chip with the control logic (Smart SIPMOS). Inside: current limit, gate protection, overvoltage protection, a voltage sensor, level shifter and rectifier, output voltage detection, a temperature sensor, a limit for unclamped inductive loads, ESD protection on the input and the current sense stage. The logic is fed from Vbb through Rbb.
Switching resistive, inductive and capacitive loads returned to ground on 12 V and 24 V DC supplies, with current-sense feedback; it takes the place of relays, fuses and discrete switch circuits.

The input is current controlled: a switch from IN to ground that can sink IIN(on) (2.2 mA max) turns the output on, and less than 30 µA leaves it off. Above Vbb = 16 V the input slew rate dVbIN/dt is rated at 20 V/µs; a series resistor RIN in the input line limits it.
Pins 1 and 5 are both OUT and must be joined outside. Two or more devices can be put in parallel for more load current; RIS is then 1 kΩ divided by the number of devices.

With a falling supply the switch stays on until VbIN falls below VbIN(u) (2.5 V typ); a short dynamic dip that does not reach VbIN(u) leaves it on. With a rising supply the charge pump restarts once Vbb passes Vbb(ucp) (4 V typ). With the input off, OUT stays low until Vbb exceeds the clamp VON(CL), after which the output follows Vbb minus the clamp.

In normal on-state IS sources IL / kILIS, about 1/10 000 of the load current, as long as VOUT - VIS stays above 5 V; RIS turns it into a voltage. Sense works from IL(MIN) = 50 mA upward. The ratio spreads more at low load current; calibrating kILIS for each device makes it more accurate. The output saturates at IIS,lim (4 to 7.5 mA). An unused IS pin can be left open. With large RIS, VIS can rise nearly to Vbb.

IS gives no valid reading during the settling time tson(IS) after turn-on, during turn-off, and for tslc(IS) after a change of load current. While VbIS stays below VZ,IS the sense current does not exceed IIS,fault or IIS,lim.

With the input on, overload, short circuit to ground and overtemperature drive IS to the fixed fault current IIS,fault (5.2 mA typ). With the input off IS carries only the leakage IIS(LL). An open load with the input on gives about IIS(LH); a short to Vbb gives less than the nominal sense current.

Overload is VON above 1 V typ while below the short-circuit level. As load current rises, the sense current climbs to IIS,lim; once VON passes about 1 V it drops to IIS,fault. The output stays on until the input is switched off.

Switching on into a short: the current rises to the limit IL(SC) and, if VON stays above VON(SC) (3.5 V typ), the device shuts down after td(SC1) (650 µs typ). IIS goes to IIS,fault after tdelay(fault). The shutdown is latched until the input current is taken to zero.

A short arriving while on: once VON passes VON(SC), the switch turns off after td(SC2) (2 µs typ); the current peak before that depends on the outside impedance. IIS goes to IIS,fault and the shutdown stays latched until IIN = 0.

The current limit falls in steps as VON rises: at 25 °C about 105 A at VON = 6 V, 75 A at 12 V, 55 A at 18 V, 40 A at 24 V and 25 A at 30 V. Above VON(SC) the internal short-circuit detection switches the device off.

A short is modelled as a primary impedance (5 µH, 10 mΩ in the supply) plus a secondary inductance LSC and resistance RSC in the output line. Full protection for a single short needs a secondary resistance at least as large as the minimum allowed for the given LSC and supply voltage; full short-circuit protection holds up to Vbb = 30 V.

At Tjt (175 °C typ, 150 °C min) the output turns off and IS gives IIS,fault while the input is on. It turns back on by itself once the junction has cooled by the hysteresis (10 K typ), cycling while the fault and input remain.

At turn-off of an inductive load the output is pulled below ground until VON reaches the clamp VON(CL), 42 V typ, and the energy is absorbed in the device. The largest load inductance for one switch-off falls with load current: about 1000 mH at 1.2 A, 6 mH at 10 A and 0.02 mH at 100 A (Tj,start = 150 °C, Vbb = 12 V, RL = 0 Ω). EAS is 0.3 J at 20 A, Tj = 150 °C.

Zeners of 67 V typ protect IN and IS (VZ,IN, VZ,IS), and the logic is fed through Rbb (100 Ω typ); the ESD zener on IN takes 15 mA max. A supply above the 67 V level can push the voltage between IS and ground past 5 V unless RV and a zener VZ,VIS are added on the sense line.

With a reversed supply the device turns its power MOSFET on, so it conducts with RON(rev) rather than through the body diode. The current into IN and IS together should be about 80 mA to keep dissipation low; it can be supplied by a small diode across the input switch, a MOSFET input switch, or by choosing RIS. Above 16 V reverse, RIN is required. The current through Rbb heats the device and counts in the thermal budget.

The device may run with VOUT > Vbb > 0 V. In this mode current sense is unavailable (IIS = 0), the intrinsic drain-source diode may conduct and dissipate much more, and there is no temperature protection. On return to forward operation switch-on can be delayed by td(inv), 1 ms typ.

operation.topic: Loss of supply with an inductive load
operation.text: If Vbb is disconnected while an inductive load is energised, the load current must be given a path that can carry it: a diode, a zener diode or a varistor across the load (inductive disconnect circuit).

Protected against load dump (45 V), loss of ground and loss of Vbb (with an outside diode when an inductive load holds energy); standby current of 3 µA typ; fast demagnetisation of inductive loads; optimised static EMC; ESD 3 kV human body model.
Green product: lead-free finish on the leads, suitable for lead-free soldering to IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020, RoHS compliant.
